previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis triggered by severe nausea and vomiting. She presented with high blood glucose, an anion gap of 28, and ketonuria, requiring ICU-level care and an insulin infusion. Her DKA resolved within 24 hours, but nausea persisted. She was managed with IV fluids, antiemetics, and close monitoring of electrolytes and blood pressure. A urinary catheter was placed due to acute retention, with resolution within 48 hours. The GI team evaluated her for possible outpatient EGD with Botox injection for gastroparesis. She gradually advanced to a regular diet, remained stable on subcutaneous insulin, and was discharged home with no medication changes and follow-up arranged with her GI physician.

Brief Hospital Course:
Patient is a ___ yo female with a history of IDDM, gastroparesis 
s/p gastric pacemaker and multiple admissions for gastroparesis 
who presents with nausea and vomiting.

#. Gastroparesis: She had severe nausea and vomiting and 
multiple admissions over the last few months for worsening 
gastroparesis.  Has gastric pacemaker that does not seem to be 
controlling her symptoms and reports some improvement with Botox 
injections during EGD in the past.  She was given IV 
anti-emetics and her home scopolamine patch.  Her nausea and 
vomiting improved the day after admission and her diet was 
advanced.  She had one further episode of vomiting on the 
morning of discharge when her blood sugar was elevated to 300's 
but tolerated lunch without difficulty and her blood sugars 
improved.  She was discharged with prn anti-emetics with plans 
to follow-up with GI in 4 days for repeat Botox injections.

#. Insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, uncontrolled, and mild 
diabetic ketoacidosis: Had anion gap of 20 in the ED after 
significant vomiting all day.  She was given SC insulin and gap 
improved to 10.  She was hydrated with normal saline which was 
changed to D5NS when BS reached 200.  She was continued on her 
home lantus 28 units at dinner and a humalog insulin sliding 
scale.  Urinalysis showed trace ketones.  Her AG continued to 
decrease and her blood sugars stabilized.

#. Tachycardia: She was tachycardic on admission likely related 
to volume depletion in the setting of significant vomiting and 
mild DKA.  ECG showed sinus rhythm.  She was maintained on her 
home metoprolol, which had to be switched to IV metoprolol 
temporarily while she was severely vomiting.

#. Hypertension: She was intermittently hypertensive but overall 
well-controlled on her home linisopril and beta blocker.  She 
was temporarily switched to IV metoprolol and enalaprilat due to 
inability to tolerate oral intake and switched back to oral 
prior to discharge.

#. GERD: Continued on home omeprazole
